title: Wave-scan attention kernel with rope-anchoring and continuous batching
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Introduces a new attention microkernel family (wave-scan) and a complementary runtime feature (rope-anchored KV entries) plus a lightweight continuous batcher. Motivation: requests with varied sequence lengths and interleaved rotary/rope offsets show degraded KV cache hit-rates and tile edge inefficiencies in our current tiling kernels. Wave-scan is a tiled attention path that minimizes tile rework by scanning key/value tiles in a wave pattern across heads and sequences, while performing rotary/rope realignment at tile boundaries (rope-anchoring). The continuous batcher holds a short-lived slot table that aggregates micro-requests across sockets for up to 6ms before dispatch; combined with adaptive priority eviction it preserves tail latency SLOs while increasing throughput for typical interactive workloads. Key design points: 1) Kernel: a new CUDA-optimized wave-scan microkernel using 2D tiling with threadgroup-wide reductions that reduces global memory writes for intermediate qk products. 2) Rope-anchoring: store a compact anchor offset with each KV cache fragment so that different rotary base offsets can reuse cached KV blocks by applying a lightweight rotation remap at load time instead of invalidating the cache. 3) Scheduler integration: the existing scheduler receives hints from the batcher about expected sequence-length distribution and sets tiling/prefetch budgets per GPU stream. 4) Eviction: priority-based eviction that favors anchored-KV blocks with high reuse probability and updates eviction score at response time. 5) Safety: fallbacks to legacy tiled-attn path when sequence-length or head-counts fall outside tested ranges. Benchmarks (internal): on A100-80GB, Llama-2-7b-like config with mixed prompt lengths (avg 256, tail 1024) we measured: - p99 latency (single-request) unchanged (+3% worst-case) with continuous batching timeout set to 6ms. - throughput (tokens/s) up 2.1x for bursty conversational workloads and 1.6x for steady-state chat load. - end-to-end cost per 1M tokens reduced ~28% on reserved capacity due to higher GPU utilization and KV reuse. Implementation notes: changed kernel is implemented in cuda/attn/wave_scan_kernel.cu with a small portability shim in kernels/warp_util.h. KV anchor metadata is a 16-bit signed offset stored alongside existing slab metadata and accessed through the kv_cache layer; minimal on-disk format change (backwards-compatible). The continuous batcher is implemented in runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cc and exposes two knobs: max_hold_ms (default 6) and slot_limit (default 128). Compatibility: all public API surfaces are unchanged; internal config adds batcher.experimental.wave_scan_enabled (off by default) and kv.cache.anchor_policy (auto|off|strict). Migration: default rollout is off; we enable it for performance lab clusters and run canary jobs before broader rollout. Checklist: - [x] microkernel implemented and unit-tested - [x] KV anchor metadata added with backward-compatible format - [x] continuous batcher integrated with scheduler hints - [x] perf benchmarks and cost model updated - [x] runtime feature flag gating - [x] docs sketch added in docs/perf/wave-scan.md Rollout plan: enable in perf-lab, run 48h canary on a subset of production-like traffic, monitor p99 latency, KV hit-rate, and eviction churn. Related work: builds on prior tiling/prefetch efforts (see ENG-1167) and complements staged prefetch scheduler prototypes (ENG-1340).

release_notes: Add experimental wave-scan attention kernel and rope-anchored KV cache to improve throughput for bursty conversational workloads. Feature is gated and off by default.
risk_assessment: Medium: kernel changes are low-level and affect memory access patterns. Feature gated, can be rolled back; added comprehensive unit and integration tests.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in production, monitor kv.cache.anchor_hit_rate, scheduling.batch_hold_ms, and p99 latency dashboards. Default gating will prevent rollout until canary passes.
